$comment: spreadsheets.values.get -> GET v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}/values/{range}, response ValueRange. Read from Google's own discovery document 2026-10-01.
title: Read Google Sheets values
description: Read the cell values of a range.

config.label: Spreadsheet ID
config.description: The long id from the sheet's URL: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/THIS_PART/edit.

config.label: Range
config.description: In A1 notation, the same shape row_append accepts.
config.$comment: Same encoding trap row_append already documents: a range contains `!` and can contain a slash (a sheet named `Q1/Q2`). Every emitter URL-encodes this.

options.label: Formatted, as shown in the sheet (e.g. "$1.50", "10/1/2026")
The underlying number or string, no formatting applied
The formula text itself, for a cell that has one

config.label: Rows or columns
config.description: Whether the outer array of the result is rows or columns.

outputShape.description: The range actually covered -- may be smaller than what was asked for; Google excludes empty trailing rows and columns.
Echoes what was asked, or ROWS by default.
Rows of cells -- an array of arrays. One row is [[a, b, c]], the same shape row_append sends. Absent entirely when the range is empty.
Which estate this ran against. Google has no sandbox, so: fake or live.
